answers.d01: 似然回答的是：固定观测到的数据，哪个参数最可能产生它？例如抛一枚硬币10次出现7次正面。若正面概率是p，出现这个结果的概率是 p⁷(1−p)³。现在把数据'7正3反'当作固定事实，把p当作变量，这个函数就叫似然函数 L(p|数据)。它在 p=0.7 处最大，这就是'最大似然估计'。注意似然虽是概率的乘积形式，但作为p的函数通常不归一，不是关于p的概率分布。后验概率则更进一步：P(p|数据) ∝ P(数据|p) × P(p)，即似然乘上先验再归一。它回答'看过数据之后，我们对p的信念如何'。若先验认为硬币多半均匀，后验的峰值会被先验往0.5方向拉，而不是停在0.7。一句话：似然是数据对参数的支持力度，后验是结合了先验知识后的最终结论。
answers.d02: An average tells you the center of a set of numbers, but not how spread out they are. Two classes can both average 70: one where everyone scores 68–72, another with scores from 40 to 99. Variance measures that spread. Recipe: (1) take each value and subtract the average — this is its deviation from center; (2) square each deviation (multiplying it by itself); (3) average those squared deviations. That's population variance: σ² = (1/N) × Σ(xᵢ − μ)². We square for two reasons: negative deviations would otherwise cancel positive ones and sum to zero, and large deviations get extra weight, which is usually what we want. Note the units get squared too (points²), so people often take the square root — the standard deviation — to get spread back in normal units.
answers.d03: 正反馈指系统输出回过头来增强输入：变化发生后被放大，再引发更大的同方向变化，形成'越…越…'的循环。例如麦克风靠近音箱，微小噪声被放大、再拾取、再放大成啸叫；复利、流感传染、冰川融化（变暖→冰减少→反射阳光少→更暖）都是同类结构。关键在于反馈方向与原变化一致，偏差被逐圈累积。但'正'只描述方向，不是价值判断：放大既可以是良性增长，也可以是失控——金融泡沫、踩踏、炎症风暴都是正反馈的恶果。与之相对的负反馈抑制变化、维持稳定（如恒温器）。因此正反馈不等于好事：它意味着远离平衡、自我强化，一旦方向不利就会迅速滑向极端，所以很多系统会刻意设计负反馈来约束它。
answers.d04: You have a free afternoon and can nap, study, or play tennis — but only one. If you choose to nap, the opportunity cost isn't 'all the things you gave up'; it's the value of the single best alternative you didn't pick, say an hour of productive study. That foregone value is the true price of the nap, even though it's free in money. Thinking this way clarifies decisions: a cheap but time-consuming choice can actually be expensive if your best alternative was valuable; conversely, an expensive movie is cheaper (in opportunity cost) on a day you had nothing better to do anyway. Key points: cost is measured by what you give up, alternatives are mutually exclusive so only the best one counts, and it includes non-monetary things like rest, learning, and fun — a beginner-friendly way to compare options on one scale.
answers.d05: 设想某种病患病率是1%，检测灵敏度99%（病人检测呈阳性的概率），假阳性率5%（健康人也有5%呈阳性）。现在某人检测阳性，他真患病的概率是多少？直觉说99%，其实不然。取10000人：约100人患病，其中99人被检出；其余9900名健康人中，5%即约495人假阳性。阳性共594人，真正患病的只有99人，概率约99/594≈17%。这就是贝叶斯公式：P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病) / P(阳性)。它把'检测有多准'（似然）和'本来就多常见'（先验）结合起来，再除以总阳性率归一。核心教训：检测准确率不等于患病概率，因为健康人基数远大于病人，假阳性会占多数。
answers.d06: A cache is a fast local copy of data that's expensive to fetch (e.g., your app stores a user's profile in memory or Redis instead of hitting the database every time). Cache invalidation is the problem of keeping that copy correct: when the underlying data changes, the cached copy becomes stale and must be deleted or refreshed. The three common strategies: (1) TTL — expire entries after, say, 60 seconds; simple, but data can be stale in between. (2) Invalidate on write — whenever you update the database, delete the matching cache key so the next read reloads fresh data. (3) Write-through — update cache and database together. It's famously hard because in a distributed system there are many cache copies and 'when exactly should each be dropped?' has no perfect answer — hence the saying that cache invalidation is one of the two hard problems in computer science.
answers.d07: 相关指两个量一起变化，因果指一个量的变化导致另一个变化，二者常被混淆。例子：某城市统计发现，冰淇淋销量越高，溺水死亡人数越多。两者确实强相关，但冰淇淋并不导致溺水。真正的原因是隐藏的第三个变量——夏天气温高：天热使人们既多买冰淇淋，也多去游泳，溺水随之增多。这类'共同原因'叫混杂因素。判断因果不能只看相关，常用办法：随机对照实验——把人随机分成吃冰淇淋和不吃两组，其他条件被随机性拉平，若溺水仍随冰淇淋增加，因果才成立（此例中不会）；时间顺序（原因须在前）；控制变量后相关是否消失；以及合理的因果机制。记住：相关是因果的必要线索，但单凭相关无法确定谁导致谁。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth on growth: each period's gain is added to the base, so future gains are computed on a bigger amount. At 10% per year, 1000 becomes 1100, then 1210, 1331… because you earn interest on your interest. The formula is final = start × (1+r)ⁿ — exponential, not linear. Over 30 years at 7%, $1,000 grows to about $7,600. Why the starting amount matters: it's the base that gets multiplied. Everyone earning 7% gets the same multiplier, so starting with twice as much ends with twice as much. Time acts like a second multiplier: the same $1,000 invested at 25 instead of 35 years old can end roughly twice as large, because the early dollars compound through more periods. Practical takeaways: start early, protect the principal, and beware of losses — a 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover, since the base shrinks.
answers.v01: 过拟合就像一个学生复习考试时不理解方法，只把练习题连同答案一字不背下来。练习题（训练数据）他全对，可考试一换数字就懵了——他背的是题目细节，不是规律。机器学习模型也会犯同样的错：模型太复杂或数据太少时，它会把训练数据里的噪声和巧合当成'规律'记下来，于是在见过的数据上表现极好，遇到新数据却很差。判断方法是留一部分数据做'考试卷'（验证集）：训练成绩高而考试成绩低，就是过拟合的典型信号。解决办法包括：收集更多数据、换更简单的模型、加正则化惩罚复杂度、早停训练。目标是学到能推广的一般规律，而不是死记硬背样本。
answers.v02: Imagine searching 100 documents, of which 10 are actually relevant. Your system returns 8 results, and 6 of them are relevant. Precision = 6/8 = 75%: of what the system returned, how much was correct. It measures 'how clean the results are' — did we waste the user's time with junk? Recall = 6/10 = 60%: of everything relevant out there, how much did we actually find. It measures 'how complete the results are' — did we miss anything important? The two can conflict: returning only the single document you are most sure of gives high precision but low recall; dumping all 100 documents gives perfect recall but terrible precision. Good search systems must balance both, depending on whether misses or false alarms are more costly.
answers.v03: 自然选择改变的是种群，而不是个体。要点有三：第一，变异是随机产生的——个体不能'努力让自己进化'，长颈鹿不会因为伸脖子就把脖子变长；变异在出生时就已存在，方向不受需求控制。第二，环境是筛子而非指导者：与生存繁殖更相关的性状，其携带者平均留下更多后代，把这些基因更多地传下去。第三，代代累积，种群中有利变异的频率上升、不利变异下降，这就是种群被'改变'的含义。例如抗生素耐药性：细菌群体中本来就有少数随机突变出抗药的个体，抗生素杀死了敏感菌，等于替抗药菌清除了竞争者，它们的频率迅速上升。不是细菌'学会'了抗药，而是筛选改变了种群构成。
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent if performing it once has the same effect as performing it many times. In distributed systems this matters because networks are unreliable: after a timeout you don't know if your request reached the server, so you retry — and the message may also be duplicated in queues. If retries are dangerous, every failure becomes a dilemma. Compare: 'set account balance to 100' is idempotent — doing it twice leaves the same state. 'Add 10 to the balance' is not — retrying double-charges. Practical techniques: (1) idempotency keys — the client sends a unique token; the server remembers processed tokens and returns the original result instead of re-executing; (2) conditional writes like 'set status to paid WHERE status = pending'; (3) deduplication by business ID so inserting the same order twice is a no-op. Designing write APIs to be idempotent by default makes retries safe.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量一个随机结果有多'不确定'：H = −Σ pᵢ·log pᵢ，即每种结果的信息量按其概率加权平均。直观上，熵等于知道结果后你平均获得的'意外程度'。为什么均匀分布最不确定？因为均匀意味着每种结果同样可能，你毫无偏向可利用，猜中的把握最小。对比两个二选一：p=0.99 时你几乎肯定能猜对，惊喜很少，熵接近零；p=0.5 时完全拿不准，熵达到最大。数学上，在'各概率加起来为1'的约束下，−p·log p 是凹函数，由不等式可证概率摊得越平，熵越大；极端集中（某结果概率为1）时熵为零，即完全确定。这就是为什么公平硬币、公平骰子最难预测。
answers.v06: A deadlock happens when processes hold resources while waiting for each other, and none can proceed. Example: Thread 1 acquires lock A (the account list), then wants lock B (the log file). Meanwhile Thread 2 acquires lock B, then wants lock A. Each holds what the other needs, so both block forever — a cycle in the resource-allocation graph. For a deadlock to occur, four conditions must all hold: mutual exclusion (resources can't be shared), hold-and-wait (a process keeps resources while waiting for more), no preemption (resources can't be forcibly taken back), and circular wait. Breaking any one condition prevents deadlock. Common fixes: impose a global lock ordering so all threads request locks in the same sequence (kills circular wait), acquire all locks atomically up front, or use timeouts and back off. Databases use this too: detecting wait-for cycles and aborting one victim transaction.
answers.v07: 公共物品是同时满足'非排他'和'非竞争'的物品：无法阻止任何人享用，且一个人用不妨碍别人用。典型例子：国防、路灯、干净的空气、防洪堤。问题在于既然人人都能免费享用，理性的个体就不愿出钱——这叫搭便车：明知别人会付费，自己坐享其成。结果人人都这么想，公共物品供给不足。经典例子：楼道照明，每户都想蹭邻居的钱。这不是道德问题，而是个人理性与集体理性的冲突。社会常用办法：政府征税强制筹资（国防、路灯），明确产权或规制（治污），把'非排他'变成'可排他'（收费的高速公路、有线电视），以及声誉和社会压力等非正式机制。
answers.v08: Little's law is a simple but powerful queueing identity: L = λW. L is the average number of items in the system, λ the average arrival rate, and W the average time an item spends in the system (waiting plus service). Example: customers arrive at 10 per minute and each spends 4 minutes in the shop; then on average L = 10 × 4 = 40 customers are inside. The intuition: every arrival stays W time units, so counting arrivals over time gives you the population. It holds for any stable system in steady state, regardless of the arrival or service distributions — no fancy assumptions needed. Practical uses: if a server handles 100 requests/second and keeps latency under 200 ms, it must be processing about 20 requests concurrently; measuring any two of L, λ, W reveals the third.
